      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "whether the fuzz test harness duplicates PR #34651",
      "quote": "have you seen https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34651 btw? from a quick skim, this fuzz test looks similar. it uses a wrapper around `ConnectBlock` instead of calling it directly. or am I missing something?",

    {
      "id": "rc:3046803139",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "test bailout check using logical AND instead of OR risks bad_optional_access if only one AddCoin call fails",
      "quote": "This uses `&&` so it only bails if both `AddCoin` calls fail. If just one fails you get a `bad_optional_access` from `.value()`. The rest of the file uses `if (!outpoint) return;` for each one individually. Should this be `||`?",

      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "fixed in push",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3046884251"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4201614356",
      "status_by_quote": "Fixed https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35000#discussion_r3046803139"
    },

      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "drop the redundant fuzz target and focus on the unit tests",
      "quote": "I agree that the fuzz test looks a bit redundant with https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34651. And I'm not sure it's worth having this PR's harness only as a way to cover the contextual checks... I think it could make sense to drop the fuzz target here and focus on the unit tests, which look well-written to me.",

      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "add the same checks through ProcessNewBlock by subscribing to the BlockChecked validation interface event",

      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "call ConnectBlock directly with invalid blocks",

      "part": 3,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "tag tests with an enum and pass through validation entry points instead of splitting into separate tests",
      "quote": "Instead of splitting them up into separate tests I am wondering if we could tag them with an enum and then pass them to various entry points of validation (i.e. TestBlockValidity, ProcessNewBlock, ConnectBlock).",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined to keep the test structure simple",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:4566407744"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4566407744",
      "status_by_quote": "Hmm, won't this be more involved? I would like to keep it simple as it is currently, if you don't feel strongly about this."
    },

      "id": "rc:3352677834",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "assert unused outpoints in AddCoin or test setup so tests fail loudly instead of returning early",
      "quote": "BOOST_REQUIRE(outpoint) seems to be more appropriate than if (!outpoint) return because the outpoint is required for the rest of the test. If helper setup fails, the test will fail immediately instead of silently passing by returning early.",

      "status_by_quote": "https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35000#discussion_r3352677834 took the second approach, it's more DRY"
    },

      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "move ResetBlock, MakeBlock, AddCoin, and SolveBlockPow into util/mining.h",
      "quote": "Could ResetBlock, MakeBlock, and AddCoin better fit as standalone functions in `util/mining.h`? Maybe `SolveBlockPow` could be moved over there as well and be called in `MineBlock` and some of the other blaces where we are mining in the tests.",

      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "remove retry loop in AddCoin and set possible_overwrite to false",

participants.note: asked whether the block validity fuzz harness duplicated PR #34651
pointed out bad_optional_access bug in test bailout check
suggested dropping redundant fuzz test in favor of unit tests, which looked well-written
Concept ACK and ACK; suggested test setup assertion improvement
Approach ACK; suggested entry points, coverage additions, and declarative test style

claims.text: whether the fuzz test harness duplicates PR #34651
claims.quote: have you seen https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34651 btw? from a quick skim, this fuzz test looks similar. it uses a wrapper around `ConnectBlock` instead of calling it directly. or am I missing something?
claims.status_note: author explained differences and acknowledged shared utilities would be useful
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks for pointing that out. I wasn’t aware of it. #34651 and the second commit in this PR, e9115735a45289a783b561fe482ab1540b03d076 have a lot in common

claims.text: test bailout check using logical AND instead of OR risks bad_optional_access if only one AddCoin call fails
claims.quote: This uses `&&` so it only bails if both `AddCoin` calls fail. If just one fails you get a `bad_optional_access` from `.value()`. The rest of the file uses `if (!outpoint) return;` for each one individually. Should this be `||`?

claims.text: drop the redundant fuzz target and focus on the unit tests
claims.quote: I agree that the fuzz test looks a bit redundant with https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34651. And I'm not sure it's worth having this PR's harness only as a way to cover the contextual checks... I think it could make sense to drop the fuzz target here and focus on the unit tests, which look well-written to me.
claims.status_note: author pruned redundant fuzz harness in push
claims.status_by_quote: Pruned the fuzz harness added here in favour of the one in #34651

claims.text: move test utilities into the new block_validity util module
claims.quote: Why not put these into the new block_validity util module?
claims.status_note: author resolved test util module placement in push

claims.text: add the same checks through ProcessNewBlock by subscribing to the BlockChecked validation interface event
claims.quote: Can we add the same checks through `ProcessNewBlock` by subscribing to the `BlockChecked` validation interface event?
claims.status_note: author implemented ProcessNewBlock checks in push

claims.text: call ConnectBlock directly with invalid blocks
claims.quote: As an addition I would also be interested in calling `ConnectBlock` directly with these invalid blocks.
claims.status_note: author added ConnectBlock tests in push

claims.text: tag tests with an enum and pass through validation entry points instead of splitting into separate tests
claims.quote: Instead of splitting them up into separate tests I am wondering if we could tag them with an enum and then pass them to various entry points of validation (i.e. TestBlockValidity, ProcessNewBlock, ConnectBlock).
claims.status_note: author declined to keep the test structure simple
claims.status_by_quote: Hmm, won't this be more involved? I would like to keep it simple as it is currently, if you don't feel strongly about this.

claims.text: assert unused outpoints in AddCoin or test setup so tests fail loudly instead of returning early
claims.quote: BOOST_REQUIRE(outpoint) seems to be more appropriate than if (!outpoint) return because the outpoint is required for the rest of the test. If helper setup fails, the test will fail immediately instead of silently passing by returning early.
claims.status_note: author centralized assertion inside AddCoin in push
claims.status_by_quote: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35000#discussion_r3352677834 took the second approach, it's more DRY

claims.text: move ResetBlock, MakeBlock, AddCoin, and SolveBlockPow into util/mining.h
claims.quote: Could ResetBlock, MakeBlock, and AddCoin better fit as standalone functions in `util/mining.h`? Maybe `SolveBlockPow` could be moved over there as well and be called in `MineBlock` and some of the other blaces where we are mining in the tests.

claims.text: remove retry loop in AddCoin and set possible_overwrite to false
claims.quote: A collision seems unlikely to me given we are streaming 256 bits from the chacha keystream. Even if so, would trying again five times really help? The `possible_overwrite` argument could also be set to `false` (and should get a `/*=*/` arg comment).

claims.text: clarify what belongs in the contextual check tests versus ConnectBlock tests
claims.quote: I'm a bit confused about what exactly should be in this file. The comment says this should cover `ContextualCheckBlock`, but some of these are only called in `ConnectBlock`, like this one and `bad-cb-amount`, and others like the witness malleation checks are in another file.

claims.text: drop TestBlockValidity-specific check covered by functional tests
claims.quote: Should we really be checking this here? It's probably one of the few things that are purely `TestBlockValidity` specific and is already covered by a functional test.

claims.text: explain if the loop in header tests is needed due to non-deterministic setup
claims.quote: Is this loop really needed? Is there something non-deterministic about the setup here?

claims.text: add a unit test for timewarp
claims.quote: Do you want to add a test for timewarp?

claims.text: remove redundant block-script-verify-flag-failed cases covered by interpreter tests
claims.quote: Isn't one case exercising the `block-script-verify-flag-failed` failure enough? The other script failure cases should already be covered exhaustively in the interpreter tests.

claims.text: add a test checking coinbase amounts for a block with fees and multiple coinbase outputs
claims.quote: Might it be interesting to add another test that checks coinbase amounts for a block with some fees and multiple coinbase outputs?

claims.text: check transaction chains within a block
claims.quote: Could this be extended with a check for chains of transactions within a block?

claims.text: add a case exercising SequenceLocks failure
claims.quote: Can you add a case here that exercises the SequenceLocks failure ("contains a non-BIP68-final transasction")?

claims.text: consider moving toward a declarative, vectorized test style
claims.quote: If we want to add way more cases for exercising edge cases and boundary conditions, then I could see the benefits for a more declarative, vectorized style. What are your thought on this?

claims.text: use integer arithmetic COIN * 9 / 10 instead of floating-point 0.9 * COIN for CAmount
claims.quote: 0.9 * COIN uses floating-point arithmetic. COIN * 9 / 10 is evaluated as (COIN * 9) / 10, using integer arithmetic throughout, which fits CAmount better.
claims.status_note: applied by author in commit ccfc34482d1120aa05d65c83d3e41f8dbee851b3

claims.text: remove redundant comment since inheriting from TestChain100Setup is self-explanatory
claims.quote: This comment seems redundant, inheriting from TestChain100Setup seems enough of an explainer to me.

claims.text: whether the comment describing returning a template instead of a block is outdated
claims.quote: Is this comment outdated? Looks like it is returning a block now, not a template.

claims.text: whether the test comment should say exceeds the block height
claims.quote: Should this say exceeds the block height?
